dream: I lay the dark oak down on the wedge, but the oak melted into a puddle of dark ink. I pressed the flat anchor into the mess, trying to catch the slip that now slid sideways through the ink. The air felt thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I could not touch. I waited for the wedge to bite, but it just lay tired and flat. Then the card boiled, turning my own hand into steam, and I woke up with a fresh, smooth corner where my rough grip had been.
